title: Identifying Neural Dynamics Using Nonlinear Interventional State Space Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.08113v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: State-space models (SSMs) recover low-dimensional latent dynamics from high-dimensional observations, but latents are generally not identifiable from observational data alone. Interventional state-space models (iSSMs) use perturbations to break observational symmetries and identify parameters up to permutation, scaling, and shift. However, prior work restricts identifiability to linear latent dynamics and piecewise-linear emissions, excluding many behaviors characteristic of neural circuits. We extend iSSMs to a substantially broader model class: we prove that (i) affine identifiability holds under general injective emission functions and Gaussian latent transitions, and (ii) with interventions, identifiability up to permutation, scaling, and shift is preserved under general nonlinear latent dynamics. We validate our theory on simulated FitzHugh-Nagumo dynamics, and then demonstrate two applications: adjudicating between competing mode

translated_title: 使用非线性干预状态空间模型识别神经动力学
translated_abstract: 状态空间模型（SSMs）能够从高维观测数据中恢复低维潜在动力学，但仅凭观测数据通常无法识别这些潜在变量。干预状态空间模型利用扰动打破观测对称性，从而在允许置换、缩放和平移的等价意义下识别模型参数。然而，先前的工作将可识别性限制在线性潜在动力学和分段线性发射函数，排除了神经回路中许多典型的行为特征。我们将iSSMs扩展到更广泛的模型类别：我们证明（i）在一般的单射发射函数和高斯潜在转移下，仿射可识别性成立；（ii）在有干预的情况下，在一般的非线性潜在动力学下，直到置换、缩放和平移的可识别性仍然保持。我们在模拟的FitzHugh-Nagumo动力学上验证了该理论，随后展示了两个应用：在相互竞争的模型之间进行裁决……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究将干预状态空间模型的可识别性理论从线性动力学推广到一般非线性潜在动力学与单射发射函数，为识别神经回路动力学提供了更广泛的理论保证。
en_tdlr: This work extends the identifiability guarantees of interventional state-space models from linear dynamics to general nonlinear latent dynamics and injective emission functions, providing a substantially broader theoretical foundation for identifying neural circuit dynamics.
